steps.tx: Gastro-oesophageal malignancies display distinct anatomical distributions and histology. Adenocarcinoma predominates in the distal oesophagus and junction, driven by Barrett metaplasia, while squamous carcinoma associates with smoking and alcohol. The **Siewert classification** categorises adenocarcinoma of the gastro-oesophageal junction into type 1 distal oesophagus, type 2 true cardia, and type 3 subcardial gastric origin, dictating thoracic versus transhiatal surgical planning.

steps.tx: Locally advanced resectable oesophageal cancer benefits from multimodal neoadjuvant therapy. In the landmark **CROSS trial**, neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy with carboplatin and paclitaxel plus 41.4 Gy radiation significantly improves overall survival in resectable oesophageal and GEJ cancer. The regimen achieved a pathological complete response rate of forty-nine percent in squamous cell carcinomas and twenty-three percent in adenocarcinomas, with manageable perioperative morbidity.

steps.tx: Patients failing to achieve pathological complete response face high recurrence rates. In **CheckMate 577**, adjuvant nivolumab for 1 year significantly doubles disease-free survival in resected oesophageal or GEJ cancer with residual pathological disease after neoadjuvant chemoradiation. Median disease-free survival reached 22.4 months with nivolumab compared to 11.0 months with placebo, establishing adjuvant immunotherapy as the global post-operative standard.

steps.tx: For gastric and gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinomas, perioperative chemotherapy optimizes curative-intent resection. In the German AIO **FLOT4** trial, perioperative FLOT fluorouracil, leucovorin, oxaliplatin, docetaxel 4 cycles pre- and post-operatively improves overall survival compared to ECF/ECX in gastric and GEJ adenocarcinoma. Median survival extended from 35 to 50 months, establishing triplet chemotherapy as the reference perioperative approach worldwide.

steps.tx: Molecular biomarker evaluation dictates targeted therapy additions in unresectable advanced adenocarcinoma. In the **ToGA trial**, trastuzumab added to cisplatin and fluoropyrimidine significantly prolongs overall survival in untreated HER2-positive advanced gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma. Benefit was greatest in high-expressing tumours with immunohistochemistry 3-plus or IHC 2-plus with positive in situ hybridization, extending median overall survival to 16 months.

steps.tx: The glands show **gastric adenocarcinoma** with strong **HER2** staining along basolateral membranes and a pale unstained luminal surface. This U shaped pattern defines HER2 positivity under ToGA criteria. Identifying it matters because HER2 positive advanced cancer benefits from adding **trastuzumab** to chemotherapy, with the greatest survival gain in strongly positive tumors.
steps.say: This micrograph shows gastric glands with strong HER2 membrane staining on the sides and base of cells while the luminal surface stays unstained. Under ToGA criteria this basolateral pattern marks HER2 positive gastric or junctional adenocarcinoma. Testing matters because adding trastuzumab to chemotherapy prolongs survival in HER2 positive advanced disease, especially with strong expression.

steps.tx: Claudin 18.2 represents a novel tight-junction target exposed upon malignant transformation of gastric mucosa. **Zolbetuximab**, a monoclonal antibody targeting Claudin 18.2, combined with chemotherapy significantly improves PFS and OS in Claudin 18.2-positive, HER2-negative advanced gastric adenocarcinoma in SPOTLIGHT. Eligibility requires moderate-to-strong membranous Claudin 18.2 expression in at least seventy-five percent of tumour cells.

steps.tx: Immune checkpoint blockade provides survival benefits in PD-L1 expressing advanced disease. In **CheckMate 649**, first-line nivolumab added to FOLFOX or CAPOX significantly prolongs overall survival in advanced gastric and GEJ cancer with PD-L1 combined positive score CPS 5 or higher. In CPS 5 or higher populations, median overall survival reached 14.4 months with nivolumab plus chemotherapy compared to 11.1 months with chemotherapy alone.

steps.tx: Adequate surgical nodal clearance is critical to prevent locoregional recurrence and ensure accurate staging. **D2 lymphadenectomy** dissecting perigastric nodes and nodes along the celiac axis and branches is the gold-standard surgical oncological procedure for curative gastric cancer resection. It requires harvesting a minimum of sixteen, and preferably more than thirty lymph nodes, while preserving spleen and pancreatic tail.

steps.tx: The operative view highlights green nodal packets around the stomach plus the **hepatic artery**, **coeliac axis**, and splenic artery chains beside pancreas and spleen. This matters because the lesson defines **D2 clearance** as removal of perigastric nodes with those regional basins for staging and local control, with an adequate node harvest while sparing nearby organs.
steps.say: The image shows an open abdomen with labeled nodal groups around the stomach and along major nearby arteries over the pancreas toward the spleen. It reinforces the lesson standard of extended nodal clearance for curative stomach surgery to improve staging and reduce regional relapse while preserving the spleen and pancreatic tail where possible.
